c11_acc_cbse_04_008: Contra entries are already complete inside the cash book — don't post them again to Cash and Bank ledger accounts or you'll double the effect.
c12_acc_cbse_04_010: When a partner takes over an asset, debit their Capital (claim shrinks) and credit Realisation (value received). Track the claim, not the asset's movement.
c11_acc_cbse_04_009: Individual supplier and customer accounts get posted daily — only the totals go to Purchases, Sales and GST accounts. Check your ledger folios are filled.
c12_acc_cbse_05_001: Preference shares pay a fixed dividend, but it's an appropriation of profit — holders are owners, not creditors. Unlike debenture interest, skipping it isn't default.
c11_acc_cbse_05_001: The add/deduct direction depends on your starting balance and whether the item pushes it above or below the target — don't just memorise 'add to cash book'.
c12_acc_cbse_05_002: Public, private or rights issue — the journal mechanics are identical (Application → Allotment → Calls). Only the source of the money and paperwork differ.
c11_acc_cbse_05_002: The bank debits your account when the cheque is presented and paid — not when you issued it. Check presentation dates when reconciling.
c12_acc_cbse_05_003: Share Capital is always credited at face value — a ₹10 discount on a ₹100 share goes to Discount on Issue, and premium belongs in Securities Premium Reserve.
c11_acc_cbse_05_003: 'Deposited but not collected = deduct' only holds when you start from the cash book — starting from the passbook or an overdraft flips the sign. Check the start point.
c12_acc_cbse_05_004: In pro-rata allotment the excess application money isn't refunded first — it goes toward allotment, then calls, and only the leftover is returned.
c11_acc_cbse_05_004: Bank charges and bank-credited interest appear in the passbook first — the cash book is lagging. Update the cash book, then reconcile.
c12_acc_cbse_05_005: Calls in Arrears isn't just netted off on the Balance Sheet face — deduct it in the Notes under Share Capital and show it under Current Assets.
c11_acc_cbse_05_005: Money reaching the bank doesn't update the cash book — they're separate records. A direct deposit raises the passbook first; you still must enter it yourself.
c12_acc_cbse_05_006: Debit the asset at the agreed purchase consideration, not the shares' face value — the difference is what adjusts Securities Premium or Discount.
c11_acc_cbse_05_006: A dishonoured cheque means the bank reversed the credit — subtract that amount from the cash book balance to reach the lower passbook figure.
c12_acc_cbse_05_007: On forfeiture, debit Securities Premium only if the premium was never received — premium already collected stays put. Credit Forfeited Shares with the amount actually paid.
c11_acc_cbse_05_007: Not every cash book error needs a journal entry first — an unrectified error is adjusted in the BRS itself; bank's own errors never get a journal entry at all.
c12_acc_cbse_05_008: On re-issue, discount is limited to the forfeited amount per share and debited to Forfeited Shares — gains go to Capital Reserve, not Securities Premium.
c11_acc_cbse_05_008: 'Unpresented cheques = add' flips under an overdraft — your cash book overdraft is higher than the bank's, so deduct to match. Picture which balance is ahead.
c12_acc_cbse_05_009: Buyback premium isn't a P&L loss — it's a return of capital to shareholders, debited to Securities Premium then free reserves, never to profit.
c11_acc_cbse_05_009: Adjustment signs aren't fixed per item — they flip with the starting point and with overdrafts. Always ask: does this item make my starting balance higher or lower?
c12_acc_cbse_05_010: Paid-up capital isn't just issued minus arrears — account for under-subscription, called-up amounts, the paid-up part of forfeited shares, and calls in advance as a liability.
c11_acc_cbse_05_010: Overdraft reconciliation isn't just a minus sign on the start — every add/deduct flips. Unpresented cheques mean the bank shows less overdraft, so deduct.
c12_acc_cbse_06_001: Secured/unsecured asks whether a charge exists; first/second asks the charge's ranking. Second debentures can still be secured — check which question is being asked.
c11_acc_cbse_06_001: A tallied Trial Balance isn't proof of correctness — errors of principle, omission and compensating errors can all hide inside equal columns. Keep checking anyway.
c12_acc_cbse_06_002: Debentures are credited at face value even when issued at a discount — debit the discount separately; it's a capital loss, not a revenue expense like discount allowed.
c11_acc_cbse_06_002: A zero-balance account still belongs in the Trial Balance — show it with zero in its normal column to keep the audit trail complete.
c12_acc_cbse_06_003: Divide the purchase consideration by the issue price, not face value — at a 10% discount a ₹100 debenture brings only ₹90, so you need more of them.
